structured.approach: I read the TSK-07 Frontend task in feat.tasks to see what the change touches: one render helper, the version in package.json and the test file, with no transport. I checked that against the tool view for the restricted permission table, which says no secrets are required or granted for ap_portal. I also read the ap_portal code, CI script, package.json and test imports to confirm nothing reads a secret. Required and granted secrets match (none on either side), so I raised no access request and wrote task.secrets_scope with names only.

claims.text: The Frontend task TSK-07 (STORY-07) changes only src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json (version only) and tests/portal.test.js in ap_portal.
TSK-07 depends only on the CT-1 field list, and the design adds no transport layer, so the frontend task calls no service.
No secrets are required or granted for the ap_portal repository according to the permission table.
ap_portal's package.json declares no dependencies, so no package registry token is needed.
The current ap_portal source reads no environment variable and calls no external service.
The CI script sets only NODE_PATH to 'src' on top of the process environment and reads no secret.
The portal tests load only node:test, node:assert and ap_portal.
Required and granted secrets match (none), so no access request is raised and the task can go ahead.

structured.summary: The Frontend task for FEAT-ZD-48600 (TSK-07, ap_portal) needs no secrets in local, dev or main. The permission table also grants none, so no access request was needed. I wrote task.secrets_scope.md with names only. It sets one re-entry condition: if a transport, external API or token-gated dependency is added later, FE-02 runs again.
